pointers.sentence: `--merge`, `--empty` and `--update` each leave that road at one point; `--dry-run`, `--check` and `--scriptable` change what is written, asked and printed along it (`django/core/management/commands/makemigrations.py:Command.handle`).
`Command.handle` makes its loader as `MigrationLoader(None, ignore_no_migrations=True)` (`django/core/management/commands/makemigrations.py:Command.handle`).
With no connection the loader asks no database what has been applied and counts nothing as applied (`django/db/migrations/loader.py:MigrationLoader.build_graph`).

`ignore_no_migrations=True` quiets two errors of [Finding migrations: `MigrationLoader`](loader.md): an application for which `MIGRATION_MODULES` names a module that is not there is counted as unmigrated, and a dependency on `"__first__"` or `"__latest__"` of a migrated application with no migration yet is dropped (`django/db/migrations/loader.py:MigrationLoader.load_disk`, `django/db/migrations/loader.py:MigrationLoader.check_key`).

`ignore_no_migrations=True` quiets two errors of [Finding migrations: `MigrationLoader`](loader.md): an application for which `MIGRATION_MODULES` names a module that is not there is counted as unmigrated, and a dependency on `"__first__"` or `"__latest__"` of a migrated application with no migration yet is dropped (`django/db/migrations/loader.py:MigrationLoader.load_disk`, `django/db/migrations/loader.py:MigrationLoader.check_key`).

On the others `MigrationLoader.check_consistent_history` reads the database's table and raises `InconsistentMigrationHistory`, which ends the command, if a migration applied there, and in the loader's graph, has a parent, a migration it depends on, that is not applied there (`django/db/migrations/loader.py:MigrationLoader.check_consistent_history`).

An unapplied parent is let pass where it is a replacing migration each of whose replaced migrations is applied or is, in turn, such a replacing migration (`django/db/migrations/loader.py:MigrationLoader.all_replaced_applied`).

`handle` gives `ConnectionRouter.allow_migrate` the hint `model_name` as the model's `Options.object_name`, the class's name with its capitals, where `ConnectionRouter.allow_migrate_model` and `MigrationExecutor.detect_soft_applied`, its other callers that give the hint, give the lower-case `Options.model_name` (`django/db/models/options.py:Options.contribute_to_class`).

If it answers `None` to a name it does not know, the history is checked even of a database it keeps every model out of: with no answer from a router, `allow_migrate` returns `True` (`django/db/utils.py:ConnectionRouter.allow_migrate`; [Routing between databases: `ConnectionRouter`](../backends/routers.md)).

For makemigrations, `MigrationLoader.detect_conflicts` gives, for each application with more than one leaf node, those nodes' names (`django/db/migrations/loader.py:MigrationLoader.detect_conflicts`); where labels were given on its command line, the command drops other applications' conflicts.

If any is left and `--merge` was not given, the command stops with a `CommandError` that names them: the docstring of `MigrationGraph.leaf_nodes` calls more than one leaf in an application an error, usually the result of a merge in version control, that needs the user (`django/db/migrations/graph.py:MigrationGraph.leaf_nodes`).
With `--merge` and none left, it logs that there is nothing to merge and returns (`django/core/management/commands/makemigrations.py:Command.handle`).
With `--merge`, `Command.handle_merge` takes each application in conflict in turn (`django/core/management/commands/makemigrations.py:Command.handle_merge`).

Without `--merge`, `Command.handle` next chooses a questioner (`django/core/management/commands/makemigrations.py:Command.handle`): an `InteractiveMigrationQuestioner` unless `--noinput` was given, and then a `NonInteractiveMigrationQuestioner`.

`MigrationAutodetector.changes` is called with the loader's graph, the value of `--name`, and the labels twice, or `None` twice where there were none (`django/db/migrations/autodetector.py:MigrationAutodetector.changes`).

The loader counts such an application as **unmigrated**, and the from-state is given the unmigrated applications as its `ProjectState.real_apps` (`django/db/migrations/loader.py:MigrationLoader.project_state`): the autodetector leaves their models out of the comparison unless the label is one of those to convert ([The autodetector: comparing two project states](autodetector.md)).

A graph with no leaf node gives a from-state with no `real_apps`, so in a project with no migration at all every application's models are compared (`django/db/migrations/graph.py:MigrationGraph.make_state`).

It requires a label, and for each it makes a `Migration` with no operations, puts them in a dictionary of the shape `changes` returns, and hands that to `MigrationAutodetector.arrange_for_graph` for a number, a name and a dependency on the application's leaf node, where it has one (`django/db/migrations/autodetector.py:MigrationAutodetector.arrange_for_graph`, `django/db/migrations/migration.py:Migration`).

It requires a label, and for each it makes a `Migration` with no operations, puts them in a dictionary of the shape `changes` returns, and hands that to `MigrationAutodetector.arrange_for_graph` for a number, a name and a dependency on the application's leaf node, where it has one (`django/db/migrations/autodetector.py:MigrationAutodetector.arrange_for_graph`, `django/db/migrations/migration.py:Migration`).

`Command.write_migration_files` takes a dictionary from a label to that application's migrations, an application at a time (`django/core/management/commands/makemigrations.py:Command.write_migration_files`).

For each migration it makes a `MigrationWriter`, one that writes no header comment under `--no-header`, and, at verbosity 1 or more, logs the file's path and a line for each operation: `Operation.formatted_description`, the sign of its `Operation.category`, or `"?"` where it has none, and what its `Operation.describe` returns (`django/db/migrations/operations/base.py:Operation.formatted_description`).
At the end, as after a merge, `run_formatters` runs the formatter black over the files written, if a program of that name is on the path (`django/core/management/utils.py:run_formatters`).

`--scriptable` sends everything the command logs, with the questioner's prompts, to standard error, and each file's path to standard output: `Command.log`, through which the logged lines are written, takes its stream from `Command.log_output` (`django/core/management/commands/makemigrations.py:Command.log_output`).

With `--update` the changes are folded into each application's leaf migration by `Command.write_to_last_migration_files` (`django/core/management/commands/makemigrations.py:Command.write_to_last_migration_files`).

The new name is the first four characters of the old, an underscore, and the value of `--name` or else `Migration.suggest_name` of the rewritten migration (`django/db/migrations/migration.py:Migration.suggest_name`); where that is the old name again, `"_updated"` is added to it, so the name always changes, and the new file is never the one about to be removed.
